briefHtml:
NAV S$10,325,216 — washout Monday absorbed (watcher −0.49%; ≈−0.09% vs the restated Sep 28 base) · listed flag −2.631% · SEVEN critical riskFlags (first after 6 clean days) · Sep 28 restated −S$33.7k (four nights: ~S$73k; restated NAV = new September low)

  • Biggest mover: metals and miners broke. Trump rejected Iran's 7-day Hormuz/nuclear plan; oil re-spiked (WTI topped $96, Brent touched $100, closed $93.31 +0.98% as Saudi restored the East-West pipeline to ~3.5M bpd); 10y printed 5.24% — new high since mid-2007 (30y 5.56%, highest since 2004). Silver −5.5% (SLV $54.95; spot est ~$60.8 — the $62–64 reload zone BROKE), gold −3.9% (spot ~$4,115), GDX −5.36% to $87.89, SILJ −5.54% to $27.60. US equities fell (S&P −0.77% to 7,683.69, Nasdaq −0.92%, VIX 16.07 +8.07%); semis led down (Meta −4.8%, Intel −5.7%) — NVDA +1.7% on a record $150bn buyback. The surprise: HK did not follow — HSI +0.54% and Tencent reclaimed the 439 tell (439.80, +0.73%) on the first full-flow session; SMIC −3.63%.
  • The one thing: the Iran relief leg is off, and escalation has a date. Trump rejected Tehran's conditional offer; told Axios talks resume this week; per TE, told aides he expects US strikes on Iran to resume after November's midterms. Door left open (sanctions relief + frozen funds for concrete nuclear progress). Market read: no quick de-escalation, oil premium stays, inflation leg alive into PCE Wednesday and NFP Friday; October-hike odds ~65% (TE) to over 70% (CME). Today: RBA decides 12:30pm SGT — all 29 Bloomberg-survey economists tip a hike to 4.60%; mainland China shuts Thursday for Golden Week.

Risk flags — SEVEN critical (with a data caveat)

  • Flags: SMIC −6.9% · Xiaomi −6.2% · GDX −6.9% · SILJ −7.4% · SLVP −7.1% · CDL −6.2% · Silver −5.0% leveraged line (equity ~−7.4%). Caveat: verified closes are smaller — SMIC −3.63%, Xiaomi −0.15%, CDL −2.38%, GDX −5.36%, SILJ −5.54%; only the silver flag checks out. Duplicate values across unrelated names suggest a watcher mapping glitch; the washout itself is real.
  • Silver line (est): 1,777 oz × ~$60.8 × 1.2773 ≈ S$138.0k vs S$56.24k loan ≈ 1.69x → equity ≈ S$81.8k, −7.4 to −9% on the day; the −10% equity flag (≈ −6.7% silver day) was approached, not tripped — one more day like Monday trips it
  • Zone broken: silver est ~$60.8 is below the $62–64 reload zone for the first time; SILJ −11% from Tuesday's $31.09 peak; reload playbook suspended until $62 is reclaimed or a new base forms; next tells $60 spot and gold ~$4,100
  • Tell repaired, marginally: Tencent reclaimed 439 (439.80 +0.73%) with southbound flow back; SMIC/Xiaomi did not confirm; Golden Week thins the tape from Thursday
  • Rates/FX/quirks: 10y 5.24% / 30y 5.56%, October 65–70%+ · 4th restatement, largest yet (−S$33.7k; ~S$73k over 4 nights) · ~35% NW non-SGD (USDSGD 1.2773, USDCNY ≈ 6.71) · L46.SI 13th session · SLVP frozen a 4th session · Taiwan print stale · ~62% liquid book idle cash — vindicated again (listed −2.63% vs NAV −0.09% real)

Alpha — signals, not advice

  • HK AI barbell (Asia 10% vs ~3%; AI 15% vs ~1%): Tencent's 439 reclaim on full flow technically fires the tranche trigger, but SMIC −3.63%, Golden Week from Thursday and PCE Wednesday make the window hostile — half-tranche at most pre-PCE, full confirmation after Wednesday; failure line 425.
  • Defense sleeve (15% vs ~0%): 10y 5.24% / 30y 5.56% = deepest levels of the cycle, but the quick-de-escalation path closed (Iran rejected; strikes-after-midterms) — do not catch the knife pre-PCE; a soft PCE print is the disciplined first-tranche entry.
  • Silver/miners (real assets 20% vs ~4%): zone broken at ~$60.8; leveraged-line equity ~S$81.8k (−7.4 to −9% day); Iran sanctions-relief lever weakened but alive. No new money until $62 is reclaimed or a base forms; the −10% equity flag is the hard limit.

trumpWatch.title: Trump REJECTS Iran's 7-day Hormuz/nuclear plan; expects US strikes to resume after November midterms
trumpWatch.detail: Trump rejected Tehran's conditional offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks within 7 days (conditions were: lift the naval blockade, unfreeze assets, end the war on all fronts). He told Axios talks will resume this week, and per TradingEconomics told aides he expects US strikes on Iran to resume after November's midterm elections. He remains open to sanctions relief and release of frozen funds if concrete progress is made toward a nuclear deal. The quick-de-escalation path that drove Friday's relief bounce is off.

trumpWatch.title: Oil: WTI $93.31 +0.98% after topping $96; Brent crossed $100 intraday; Saudi East-West pipeline restored
trumpWatch.detail: The Iran rejection drove crude to session highs (WTI over $96, Brent above $100); prices trimmed after reports Saudi Arabia restored East-West pipeline flows to ~3.5M bpd following repairs — the pipeline was shut earlier this month after a drone strike launched from Iraq. Saudi-led coalition intercepted Houthi projectiles Saturday. Hormuz risk premium stays while diplomacy stalls.

trumpWatch.title: Rates: 10y prints 5.24% — new high since mid-2007; 30y 5.56% highest since 2004; October hike 65–70%+
trumpWatch.detail: TE daily print: 10y +8bp to 5.24% (Yahoo showed 5.25% at the close); 30y +1.04% to 5.56%. Traders price ~65% odds of a 25bp October hike and ~53% for December (TE); Yahoo's gold note cites CME at over 70% for October. TE cites strong data, deteriorating fiscal conditions and rising government debt; PCE (Wed) and the jobs report (Fri) are the week's deciders. Metals broke under the move: silver −5.5% (zone broken), gold −3.9%.

trumpWatch.title: NVDA the exception: record $150bn buyback + AI safety platform; AI complex otherwise hit by tight financial conditions
trumpWatch.detail: Nvidia rose 1.7% Monday after launching an AI safety platform and increasing its repurchase plan to a record $150 billion (through Jan 2028). The rest of the complex fell — Meta −4.8%, Intel −5.7%, AMD −3.6%, Micron −2.6%, MSFT −1.3%, AMZN −1.4% — as record debt issuance meets tight financial conditions; Snowflake fell on a $3.5bn convertible offering. Micron and Nike report later this week.

trumpWatch.title: RBA decides TODAY 2:30pm AEST (12:30pm SGT): all 29 Bloomberg-survey economists tip a hike to 4.60%
trumpWatch.detail: ASX rate tracker prices ~90% odds of a +25bp move to 4.60%; all four majors (CBA, Westpac, NAB, ANZ) now tip September, with ANZ tipping a further November rise. Sequencing wrinkle: August CPI lands 11:30am Wednesday — the morning AFTER the vote. No US shutdown risk: Trump signed the funding bill Sep 3 (through early December).

trumpWatch.title: Week ahead: China NBS PMI + US PCE Wednesday; Golden Week starts Thursday; ISM Thursday; NFP Friday (cons 100k)
trumpWatch.detail: Wed: Australian CPI, China NBS PMI (Sep — expected firmer; export orders improving, Korea semi exports +270% y/y in the first 10 days of September), US ADP, US GDP final Q2, US PCE (Aug). Thu: Japan Tankan Q3, US ISM Manufacturing (exp 55.0); mainland China shuts for Golden Week (Oct 1–7). Fri: Tokyo CPI, EZ CPI flash, US NFP (consensus 100k vs 162k prev; U3 4.1%).
